newsitem.title: UK: Euro bourses weaken, dollar down on rate fears.
newsitem.headline: Euro bourses weaken, dollar down on rate fears.

text.p: European stocks slipped from recent record levels and the dollar weakened sharply on Wednesday as nervous investors awaited a speech by U.S. central bank chief Alan Greenspan for clues on the direction of interest rates.

Stock markets in London, Frankfurt and Paris, which have all hit new peaks in the last few days, traded in subdued mood, encouraged by a strong close on Wall Street on Tuesday but with investors hesitant to take any risks before the keynote speech.

Currency markets saw the biggest swings with the dollar dropping by nearly two yen and half a pfennig as dealers grew jittery ahead of the testimony before the Senate Banking Committee starting at 1500 GMT.
The markets were watching for any hint on interest rates as Greenspan, Federal Reserve chairman, speaks on the health of the U.S. economy which frequently sets the pace for global growth.
The dollar's kneejerk reaction to any hint of inflation or upward pressure on rates would further weaken the U.S. currency.

"The dollar's immediate reaction to any word on higher interest rates would be negative, because it will follow the bond and equities markets," said David Bloom, currency strategist at HSBC James Capel.
Some predicted that Greenspan would not alter his position on the dangers of inflation. "I don't think he'll change his stance signficantly," said Adrian Schmidt of Chase Investment Bank.
"The Fed are biased to tighten and he'll reflect that in his comments, and say that with growth as strong as it is, the danger is that there'll be some signs of inflation in the future."

Currency markets will also be sensitive to any comments about U.S. stock prices following Greenspan's remarks last December about "irrational exuberance" in U.S. asset markets, which caused a temporary nose-dive in stocks on both sides of the Atlantic.
Although Greenspan may warn about strengthening U.S. stocks, there was doubt as to whether such a comment would drive down the market as much as it did last time, Schmidt said.
In London, stocks see-sawed in the morning session but registered a small profit by lunch-time. Analysts said any big gains would be limited ahead of Greenspan's testimony to Congress.
"I don't think people are unduly worried about Greenspan," a dealer said, noting the weaker tone of recent U.S. economic data. "But his comments will keep everyone waiting."
French stocks were weighed down by a weaker bond market that was trading quietly lower ahead of Greenspan's testimony. The blue-chip CAC-40 index slipped in and out profit during morning trade.
Frankfurt was showing a slight gain after a morning of trade that was fixated on the Greenspan testimony.
CURRENCIES AT 1200 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.6735 marks and 120.99 yen, compared with 1.6786 and 122.24 in late European trade on Tuesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1200 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 6.9 points at 4,351.6.
PARIS - The CAC-40 fell 2.78 points to 2,604.94.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was up 3.73 points at 3,236.94.
PRECIOUS METALS
GOLD was fixed at $353.85 compared with $353.35 at the London close on Tuesday.Silver was up two cents at $5.23.
